blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 25 ensures individual freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess religion.
Article 26 grants religious denominations the freedom to manage their own religious affairs.
Article 27 bars the government from compelling citizens to pay taxes for promoting any religion.
Article 28 regulates religious instruction in state-maintained educational institutions.
Articles 29 and 30 provide explicit protections to minorities regarding their culture, language, and educational institutions.
Article 27 prohibits compulsory taxation for religious promotion—frequently asked in polity MCQs.
Article 30 specifically empowers minorities to establish and administer educational institutions.
Remember that India's secularism implies equal treatment of all religions by the State.
